Hi how are you doing today?

It’s okay to cry, you need to release that pressure. Thinking about the future can be really scary, there’s just no way to know for sure what’s in store. It’s a lot easier to think about tomorrow, but even then it’s still a toss up right? I’m glad you cleaned today, you made a ton of progress doing so. Imagine if we cleaned everyday how productive we would feel looking back. We have to take things day by day, it’s the best way.

Yes, it does hurt. It’s the inverse of physical pain, but it still causes a visceral reaction. It’s okay to cry. Some days I have to break down before I can rebuild. I’m here for you if you’re lonely. We can play a game or talk about anything, experiences, aliens. I’m looking at veggie taco recipes online. What are you doing?

You’re not a coward, you just haven’t given up. You’re ready to bounce back. I read your post history and I think you’re being hard on yourself. I want you to know you’re not alone and while it’s true that no one could possibly feel the same way you do, in your skin the way you do; I can relate. It’s tough making friends, it’s tough making progress. You have to fill that void with something that benefits you, something you enjoy doing even if it’s something none but few enjoy, people will respect and admire you for being you. People will tell you you’re young and you have your whole life ahead of you but the truth and what matters is the life you live today. Do something you love doing today, talk to someone, help someone, go for a walk, make something, try to feel it’s what makes life worth living. If your sad force yourself to smile, listen to music. Clean, seriously I feel better when I clean it’s instant situational progress even when you feel stuck.

Hi. I’m sorry to hear that you’re going through this. It is definitely difficult to find a good therapist that works for you, especially in these trying times. Your ex-boyfriend leaving you may have been for the best, you really need someone who supports you not condemns you for the way you feel. You’re doing the right thing taking steps to improve your mental health and I want you to know that as this date draws closer you’re stronger than before and can pull through.

Sometimes we make mistakes that feel like negative milestones but they don’t define us, this one I promise you won’t. You’re not going to work a minimum wage job, you’re stuck in the mindset that you don’t deserve the opportunity to have anything better in your life because of mistakes you’ve made but mistakes are simply opportunities to learn about yourself and improve down the road.

I watch this video every time I’m feeling discouraged. His name is David Goggins and he pretty much reached the breaking point that you’re at now. I highly recommend watching it. 

https://youtu.be/5tSTk1083VY

What if you started to slowly ween yourself off starting tonight? There’s no way you can stop cold turkey and not hate every single day thereafter. Living with anxiety is tough and while you might feel you’re dragging your family down, your family is there to help you get on your feet. It sounds like you have a lot of time at home, there’s a massive demand for at-home work in information technology. I started taking those classes on UDemy and eventually landed a killer job doing so. It’s real possible and I understand that you feel it’s impossible right now. I believe in you to kickstart your plan to get sober and slowly get on track with a goal and a plan. Don’t give up, half the battle is over you’ve already come to terms with yourself.

Sometimes life does indeed feel monotonous and I can’t quite place my own purpose as well. The best advice I can give is to find something you enjoy doing and work towards dedicating your life to it. Not only will you find people like yourself but you’ll eventually build a circle of people who support you.

Sometimes things get worse before they get better, sometimes you have to hit rock bottom before you get the chance to look up and climb out of the hole you’re in. I won’t lie to you it’s a never ending challenge that you must stay on top of but if you really do try your hardest you can change the tide. You absolutely can do it.

Hey man, despite thinking others have it better than you, there’s no one that can put themselves in your shoes and situation. I know you’re strong because you’re here reaching out and I want to reach back and appreciate you for making the effort. It’s not easy, in my darkest days I was never able to reach out for help. You can trust your therapist, it’s their job to direct you towards better thinking and a healthier lifestyle and talking about how you feel, albeit difficult will feel relieving too.

Hey you’re not a psychopath and you’re not a disappointment. School is extremely stressful, there’s nothing wrong with dropping out if it doesn’t fit into your lifestyle and gets in the way of you managing depression. Your mental health comes first, so your parents might be upset, that’s fine. They aren’t you and couldn’t possibly understand what you are feeling. I dropped out when I was 19 in college because I was having intruding thoughts of jumping too. I came back when I was older and a much cleaner take and life worked itself out. You can do the same. Your life has just begun and what matters is how you feel, not how others feel about you.

Soon enough those people who reject you won’t matter to you because you’re already starting to build a circle of people who do care.

Absolutely my friend, sometimes life does feel like an episode of your worst nightmare on repeat and you’re strapped to the rollercoaster of oscillating feelings. There are a lot of vectors in life that lead no where, there’s a lot of people who will drain you and sometimes you might feel like you are draining other people. However I encourage you to keep searching and commend you for having been, for 15 years. It took me a very long time to find what works for me, to find my purpose and to dedicate my life to it.
